title: In re Orange
questions: Whether firing several shots at one person can support both assault and attempted murder convictions.

title: State of Washington v. Rankin
questions: Whether an officer may request the identification of a passenger in a lawfully stopped vehicle absent an articulable suspicion of criminal activity or other reasonable rationale for doing so without violating the passenger's right to privacy pursuant to Washington Constitution, article I, section 7.

title: City of Redmond v. Moore
questions: Whether the trial court properly dismissed these prosecutions for driving with a suspended license on the ground that the license suspension procedure of RCW 46.20.289 and .291 violates due process because it affords no opportunity for a hearing before the Department of Licensing.

title: Butzberger v. Foster
questions: Whether a driver who was killed when he got out of his car to go to the aid of a person trapped inside an overturned truck was “using” the overturned truck and/or his own car, for the purposes of underinsured motorist insurance.

title: American Continental Insurance v. Steen
questions: Whether a hospital’s cancellation of “claims-made” insurance policies that would have covered the hospital’s liability to a patient for a pre-cancellation injury was a retroactive annulment of insurance prohibited by RCW 48.18.320 or by public policy.

title: State of Washington v. Thomas
questions: Covell Paul Thomas appeals his conviction for aggravated first degree murder and his sentence of death. He contends that the trial court made several incorrect rulings during jury selection as well as numerous erroneous evidentiary rulings. Thomas also argues that erroneous jury instructions given during his trial violated his constitutional rights. This summary is not formulated by the Court and is provided for the convenience of the public only. title: Barrett v. Lucky Seven Saloon, Inc.
questions: Whether RCW 66.44.200(1), which prohibits the sale of alcohol to “any person apparently under the influence of liquor,” establishes a standard of liability in civil actions for damages caused by intoxicated drivers.

title: In re Grasso
questions: Vincent Grasso was convicted of sexually abusing his five-year-old daughter. He now argues that the trial judge improperly admitted into evidence several of the child’s out-of-court statements describing the abuse.

title: State of Washington v. Thompson
questions: James Ross Thompson was convicted of manufacturing methamphetamines. He argues that the evidence used to convict him was bad because the police did not have the right to (1) open his trailer door to arrest him; (2) search the trailer; or (3) search a boathouse where they found evidence of drug manufacturing.

title: Sane Transit v. Sound Transit
questions: Can Sound Transit build a 14-mile electric light rail line from downtown Seattle to Tukwila rather than build a 21-mile electric light rail line from the University District of Seattle to the City of SeaTac?

title: City of Seattle v. Mighty Movers, Inc.
questions: Mighty Movers, Inc. challenges the City of Seattle’s ordinance banning posters on utility poles and other public property. Does Seattle’s anti-posting law violate the state constitutional right to free speech?

title: State of Washington v. Porter
questions: Porter was arrested and convicted of delivery of cocaine after Seattle police conducted a successful buy-bust operation. On appeal, Porter argues that the trial court and the Court of Appeals misapplied the test used to determine whether a lesser included offense instruction is appropriate.

title: State of Washington v. Goins
questions: When a general verdict and special verdict stemming from one count are inconsistent, does the not guilty special verdict void the guilty general verdict?

title: Brooks v. State of Washington
questions: This case requires the Court to decide if an individual who is arrested under a warrant issued for someone else can sue the jail where he or she is held for failing to discover there was a misidentification.

title: State of Washington v. Carter
questions: Whether two off-duty criminal investigators needed a warrant to open and inspect a gun provided to them during a private gun handling course.

title: State of Washington v. Ramer
questions: Whether the trial court erred by finding the 11 year old defendant lacked the capacity to commit first degree rape of a child.

title: Seattle Police Officers Guild v. City of Seattle
questions: Whether the City of Seattle’s process of promoting police officers complies with the state civil service statute that requires the City to promote police officers on the basis of merit.

title: State ex rel. Citizens v. Murphy
questions: Citizens Against Tolls (CAT) challenges the State’s decision to award several contracts without a normal bidding process and to allow repayment of the motor vehicle fund that pays off state bonds with toll revenues in the Tacoma Narrows Bridge project. CAT also claims that the law allowing the Tacoma Narrows Bridge project to go forward is unconstitutional and that several errors were made by the trial judge.

title: Blaney v. International Ass'n of Machinists & Aerospace Workers
questions: The trial court found that the District discriminated against Blaney because she is a woman. Three issues concerning the money she was awarded will be discussed today: (1) was the trial court correct in telling the jury to figure out Blaney’s future wage and benefits loss from the date of the trial until her retirement, and (2) should Blaney get more money to cover the taxes she will have to pay on the money she won and (3) to pay her attorneys for the work they did on her appeal?

title: Parkland Light & Water Co. v. Tacoma-Pierce County Board of Health
questions: A number of water districts challenge the Pierce County Board of Health’s regulation requiring the water districts to add fluoride to the water.

title: State of Washington v. Kilburn
questions: A middle-school student challenges his conviction of felony harassment, claiming that his statement implying a school-shooting was intended as a joke.

title: Hangartner v. City of Seattle
questions: This case is consolidated with the previous case, Hangartner v. City of Seattle, and the primary issues are the same.

title: Safeco Insurance v. Woodley
questions: A no-fault motorist was injured in a car accident with an underinsured motorist. Her insurance company offset the amount of money owed to her under one type of coverage based on prior payments owed to her under another type of coverage. The motorist argues that because she had to pay attorneys in order to create the pool of money that allowed the insurance company to take the offset, the insurance company should pay a pro rata share of her attorney fees.

title: Hamm v. State Farm Mutual Automobile Insurance
questions: Case #1 and Case #2 share the same central issue, and are referred to as companion cases. In this case, the no-fault motorist was injured in a car accident with an uninsured motorist. The insurance company took an offset similar to the offset taken in Case #1. The motorist in this case also seeks to compel her insurance company to pay a pro rata share of her attorney fees.

title: In re Petitioners
questions: Petitioners claim that the court's decision in Andress requires vacation of their second degree felony murder convictions predicated on assault.

title: State of Washington v. Goodman
questions: Goodman was convicted of possessing methamphetamine with intent to deliver. The charging document listed the drug as “meth” rather than the full name “methamphetamine.” The court must decide if the evidence was sufficient to support the conviction and whether the use of “meth” rather than “methamphetamine” in the charging document was improper.

title: State of Washington v. Hanson
questions: Appellant Hanson claims that the court's decision in Andress requires vacation of his second degree felony murder conviction predicated on assault.

title: Estate of Otani v. Broudy
questions: This case requires the court to determine whether RCW 4.20.046, Washington’s general survival statute, allows a decedent’s estate to recover damages for a decedent’s loss of enjoyment of life, including shortened life expectancy.

title: Hisle v. Todd Pacific Shipyards Corp.
questions: Todd Pacific Shipyards and its employees signed an agreement stating that Todd’s employees would be paid 60¢ for every hour they worked from one date to another. Hisle is hundreds of Todd employees who feel they should be paid overtime (90¢ an hour) for the overtime hours they worked between the dates listed in the agreement. In addition to whether overtime should be paid, this case also addresses whether federal or state courts should hear this case, whether this case was already decided in a prior suit, and whether costs and attorney fees should be granted on appeal.

title: Arborwood Idaho v. State of Washington
questions: The City of Kennewick collects a monthly ambulance charge from every household in the city. Arborwood, a non-resident owner of apartments in Kennewick, objects to the ambulance charge.

title: Washington State Council v. Hahn
questions: Whether a court rule prohibits trial court judges from collectively bargaining with their employees?

title: Gary Anderson and Amelia Anderson, husband and wife, Appellants, v. Galvin Flying Service , a Washington corporation, Respondent

John D. Carlisle (deceased), a single man by and through Delbert D. Carlisle as the personal representative of his estate; and Delbert D. Carlisle and Myrna L. Carlisle, individually, Appellants, v. Group Health Cooperative of Puget Sound and Unknown John Does, Respondents

Nancy Loomis and Gerald Loomis, husband and wife, and as personal representatives of the Estate of Kelly Loomis, Plaintiff, v. City of Puyallup Police Department, a municipal corporation; Ambrose J. Seitz and “Jane Doe” Seitz, husband and wife; and Rodger Cool and “Jane Doe” Cool, husband and wife, Defendants
Philippides v. Bernard
questions: The parents in these four cases believe that the Legislature changed the rule in Washington that the parents of adult children can only recover for the loss of the companionship of their injured or deceased adult children if the parents were financially dependent on the children.

title: Clark v. Baines
questions: While maintaining his innocence, Wayne Baines pleaded guilty to charges that he assaulted Piety Clark. Subsequently Clark brought a lawsuit seeking damages for the assault. Baines argues Clark’s actions amount to malicious prosecution.

title: Dreiling v. Jain
questions: Whether the superior court in this shareholder derivative action properly entered a protective order allowing a report of the corporation's special litigation committee, and supporting documents, to be filed under seal.

title: State of Washington v. Heritage
questions: To protect a suspect’s constitutional right not to make incriminating confessions or admissions while in custodial interrogation by police, the Supreme Court developed warnings that an officer must give prior to interrogation. The warnings are commonly referred to as Miranda warnings. The court decides whether a suspect’s right to Miranda warnings extends to custodial interrogation by a city park security officer.

title: Urban Development, Inc., v. Dryvit Systems, Inc.
questions: A general contractor brought breach of warranty and implied indemnity claims against the manufacturer of an allegedly defective siding system used in the construction of a condominium project. The court must decide whether express warranties made through advertising can form the basis of an implied indemnity claim.

title: Port of Seattle v. Pollution Control Hearings Board
questions: Whether the Pollution Control Hearings Board properly imposed conditions upon (and, as conditioned, properly affirmed) a water quality certification issued by the Department of Ecology for the Third Runway Project at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport.

title: State of Washington v. Tuupo
questions: Should a juvenile that commits certain acts when he is 15, but is not charged until after he is 16, be automatically declined by the juvenile court and tried in adult court? Did the State violate the defendant’s due process rights by delaying prosecution until after the defendant was 18?

title: State of Washington v. Varga
questions: Whether the Legislature’s 2002 amendments to RCW 9.94.030(13) require courts to include these defendants’ prior convictions when determining their criminal histories and offender scores at sentencing for crimes they committed on or after June 13, 2002, even though defendants’ prior convictions would not have been included in their criminal histories and offender scores under the Washington State Supreme Court’s decisions in State v. Cruz, 139 Wn.2d 186, 985 P.2d 384 (1999) and State v. Smith, 144 Wn.2d 665, 30 P.3d 1245 (2001).

title: Hurd v. State of Washington
questions: The State Department of Social and Health Services maintains that the two children in these cases are no longer eligible for services for the developmentally disabled.

title: Campbell v. State of Washington
questions: The State Department of Social and Health Services maintains that the two children in these cases are no longer eligible for services for the developmentally disabled.

title: In re Dalluge
questions: This case involves issues surrounding an improper trial of a juvenile in adult criminal court, including whether trial or appellate counsel was ineffective because they failed to raise the error.

title: Mulcahy v. Farmers Insurance
questions: Mulcahy, who was insured by Farmers Ins. Co. of Washington at the time, was involved in a motor vehicle accident in British Columbia. The court must decide whether Mulcahy is entitled to receive benefits according to British Columbia’s compulsory insurance law and whether her claims that Farmers acted in bad faith and in violation of the Consumer Protection Act were properly dismissed.

title: In re Horner
questions: This court must decide whether it will hear this arguably moot case according to the continuing and substantial public interest factors. If this court decides to hear the case, then it must decide whether Joseph Horner rebutted the presumption of relocation when the trial court did not enter specific findings or discuss orally the eleven child relocation factors listed in RCW 26.09.520, and whether the Court of Appeals properly reviewed the trial court’s findings and decision for abuse of discretion.

title: Pinecrest Homeowners v. State of Washington
questions: Some Spokane homeowners have challenged a decision of the Spokane City Council that allowed a developer to move forward with a mixed-use development--one combining retail, office, and residential uses. The principal issue is whether the Council's decision misinterpreted the Spokane Municipal Code.

title: Western Farm Service, Inc. v. Olsen
questions: Key Bank has a security interest in a farmer’s potatoes. At issue is whether proceeds of the potatoes include cost of transporting potatoes paid to the farmer by a purchaser of the potatoes.

title: In re An, Attorney at Law
Thurston County v. City of Olympia
questions: Whether Thurston County may lawfully relocate its superior and district courts, as well as certain county offices, outside the county seat of Olympia to the city of Tumwater.

title: In re Isadore
questions: Can a defendant withdraw his guilty plea if he was not told prior to sentencing that he must serve community supervision after his release?

title: Staples v. Benton County
questions: Whether Benton County lawfully maintains certain offices of county government at the justice center in Kennewick.

title: Christensen v. Grant County Hospital District No. 1
questions: An employer argues that an employee should not be able to bring suit claiming he was wrongfully discharged because of his union activity when his termination was the subject of an earlier unsuccessful unfair labor practices claim.

title: In re Jones
questions: Was Russell Jones properly removed as the personal representative of his mother’s estate based on misconduct? Should James Woodard, a probate attorney, or David Jones, Russell’s brother, be appointed as the personal representative if Russell is removed? Should either party be given attorney’s fees?

title: In re Marriage of Suggs
questions: The trial court issued an order restraining Suggs from knowingly and willfully making false statements to third parties for the purpose of harassing Hamilton. The court must decide whether this civil antiharassment protection order satisfies constitutional and statutory requirements.

title: In re Personal Restraint of Addleman
questions: Did the parole board act lawfully when it denied Addleman parole?

title: Yousoufian v. Office of King County Executive
questions: What is the appropriate amount of money to award a citizen when the citizen requested documents from a county, but the county refused to release the documents in violation of state law?

title: State of Washington v. Mullin-Coston
questions: Mullin-Costin and his friend were charged with murder. His friend was tried first. The issue is what effect, if any, the jury’s verdict in the friend’s trial should have had in Mullin-Costin’s trial.

title: In re Lachapelle
questions: In these two consolidated personal restraint petitions, LaChapelle and Westfall claim their sentences do not comply with our holding in State v. Smith, 144 Wn.2d 665, 30 P.3d 1245 (2001). They seek resentencing without consideration of their juvenile offenses that “washed out” under the 1997 version of the Sentencing Reform Act.

title: Branson v. Port of Seattle
questions: Whether the concession fee that is charged to car rental companies operating at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport complies with the Municipal Airports Act, chapter 14.08 RCW.

title: In re Westfall
questions: In these two consolidated personal restraint petitions, LaChapelle and Westfall claim their sentences do not comply with our holding in State v. Smith, 144 Wn.2d 665, 30 P.3d 1245 (2001). They seek resentencing without consideration of their juvenile offenses that “washed out” under the 1997 version of the Sentencing Reform Act.

title: Castro v. Stanwood School District No. 401
questions: Does a 60-day waiting period within which a person cannot file a lawsuit against a local government entity also extend the normal deadline for filing the lawsuit by 60 days.

title: In re Higgins
questions: The Department of Corrections disciplined prison inmate David Higgins for attempting to bring drugs into the prison. Higgins appealed that decision and the Department of Corrections now seeks permission to hold a new disciplinary hearing.

title: Saddle Mountain Minerals, L.L.C. v. Joshi
questions: The Joshis own the surface of the land. Saddle Mountain owns the minerals of the same land. However, the city code appears to prohibit mining. The main issue is whether the city code renders Saddle Mountain’s minerals worthless. Also at issue is whether the surface owner’s right to have support for the surface land precludes mining and makes Saddle Mountain’s minerals worthless.

title: Kilbury v. Franklin County
questions: In light of the 2000 census, Franklin County redrew the boundaries for its three commissioner districts. This court must decide whether the County's redistricting plan complied with the statutory requirements that each district be "as compact as possible" and that district boundaries, "to the extent possible, preserve existing communities."

title: Labriola v. Pollard Group, Inc.
questions: Anthony Labriola, an employee, seeks non-enforcement of a non-compete agreement that he signed after having worked for his employer for five years.

title: In re Disciplinary Proceeding Against Dynan
questions: Did an attorney commit misconduct by submitting false evidence to the court and if so should he be suspended or disbarred?

title: State of Washington v. Maddox
questions: Were the police required to return to the judge and ask the judge to reevaluate probable cause for a search warrant after the police learned that the defendant had no methamphetamine to sell and would not have more for a couple days.

title: Judd v. American Telephone & Telegraph Co.
questions: Friends and family of prison inmates allege several telephone companies failed to provide adequate disclosure of rates for long distance telephone calls made from prisons. They seek damages under the Consumer Protection Act.

title: State of Washington v. Gaddy
questions: Whether Department of Licensing information - obtained through a police vehicle’s onboard computer - provides probable cause to arrest a defendant for driving with a suspended license.

title: Larry Carlson v. Lake Chelan Community Hospital
Carlton v. Black
questions: Myrna Black tried to admit her mother’s last will and testament to probate, though the original signed copy could never be found. The court considers whether this was proper.

title: Hodge v. Raab
questions: Whether a general liability garage policy is statutorily required to include uninsured motorist coverage.

title: In re Lord
questions: This case requires the Supreme Court to determine whether, by stipulating in his plea agreement that a prior conviction had not “washed out” and was properly included in his offender score, Lord waived his challenge that the sentencing court miscalculated his offender score when it included a “washed out” conviction. This case also requires the Supreme Court to determine whether the prosecutor breached the plea agreement when she revoked her recommendation that Lord receive Special Sex Offender Sentencing Alternative treatment instead of prison.

title: City of Seattle v. Clark-Munoz
questions: Did the state properly certify breathalyzers?

title: State of Washington v. Ross
questions: This case requires the Supreme Court to determine whether, by agreeing at sentencing that their prior out-of-state convictions and/or federal convictions were properly included in their offender scores, these defendants waived their challenge on appeal of the sentencing courts’ decisions to include their prior out-of-state and/or federal convictions in their offender scores. The Supreme Court must also determine whether the 2002 amendments to RCW 9.94A.525(12) apply retroactively to reduce Legrone’s offender score.

title: State of Washington v. Hunter
questions: This case requires the Supreme Court to determine whether, by agreeing at sentencing that their prior out-of-state convictions and/or federal convictions were properly included in their offender scores, these defendants waived their challenge on appeal of the sentencing courts’ decisions to include their prior out-of-state and/or federal convictions in their offender scores. The Supreme Court must also determine whether the 2002 amendments to RCW 9.94A.525(12) apply retroactively to reduce Legrone’s offender score.

title: In re Disciplinary Proceeding Against Romero
State of Washington v. Jagla
questions: Did the state properly certify breathalyzers?

title: City of Seattle v. Clark-Munoz
questions: Did the state properly certify breathalyzers?

title: State of Washington v. Legrone
questions: This case requires the Supreme Court to determine whether, by agreeing at sentencing that their prior out-of-state convictions and/or federal convictions were properly included in their offender scores, these defendants waived their challenge on appeal of the sentencing courts’ decisions to include their prior out-of-state and/or federal convictions in their offender scores. The Supreme Court must also determine whether the 2002 amendments to RCW 9.94A.525(12) apply retroactively to reduce Legrone’s offender score.

title: Riehl v. Foodmaker, Inc.
questions: At issue are 1) whether an employee with a disability has to show that he/she medically needs an accommodation in the workplace in order to get the accommodation and 2) whether Foodmaker fired/did not rehire Riehl because he is disabled?
result: petitioning party received a favorable disposition

title: Edelman v. State of Washington
questions: The court decides whether the Public Disclosure Commission exceeded its authority to interpret a Washington statute enacted to limit campaign contributions of large corporations and other entities.

title: Bank of America NT & SA v. David W. Hubert, P.C.
questions: At issue are (1) which bank is “the payor bank,” the bank held liable for failing to dishonor a check in a timely fashion; (2) whether Bank of America can avoid liability to Hubert P.C. by asserting that the check was fraudulently written; and (3) whether Hubert P.C. is liable to Bank of America for failing to properly supervise a paralegal.

title: In re Disciplinary Proceeding Against Egger
questions: The Bar Association Disciplinary Board has recommended that Phillip Egger be suspended from the practice of law for six months for collecting an unreasonable fee and for violating a conflict of interest rule. Both Egger and Disciplinary Counsel challenge this recommendation.

title: Keystone Land & Development Co. v. Xerox Corp.
questions: Keystone claims that the exchange of a series of letters between the parties’ brokers created a binding contract to negotiate a purchase and sale agreement for Xerox’s Tukwila, Washington facility. The Court is asked to decide whether an enforceable contract to negotiate was created, and if so what is the measure of damages for a breach.

title: In re Disciplinary Proceeding Against Guarnero
Harris v. Drake
questions: Whether the work product doctrine allows a plaintiff in a liability trial to keep from disclosure the medical report of a doctor, who was hired by his insurance company to examine him according to the terms of his automobile PIP insurance? If so, was the plaintiff too late in asserting this right when he did not tell the defendant until the day before trial?

title: City of Spokane v. Neff
questions: We decide whether the Spokane anti-prostitution ordinance is unconstitutionally vague, because the ordinance does not define the term “known prostitute.”

title: State of Washington v. Reichenbach
questions: At issue are (1) whether the police officers illegally seized drugs found in a car in which Reichenbach was riding as a passenger and (2) whether Reichenbach’s attorney failed to represent him properly and allowed him to be found guilty.

title: In re Disciplinary Proceeding Against VanDerbeek
questions: This case primarily requires the Supreme Court to determine what an attorney’s sanction should be for inflating clients’ bills.

title: State of Washington v. Throneberry
questions: Whether a judge can refuse to order a minimal sentence for a convicted criminal when the judge’s decision is based solely on his dissatisfaction with the legislature’s funding of the Department of Corrections?

title: State of Washington v. Eckblad
questions: Is Washington's seat belt law unconstitutionally vague?

title: State of Washington v. Lorenz
questions: Pamela Jean Lorenz challenges her conviction of first degree child molestation, claiming that the "to convict" instruction did not contain an essential element of the crime convicted, and that her written statement should not have been admitted because she was not given a Miranda warning. 1:00 P.M.

title: In re An, Attorney at Law
In re An, Attorney at Law
Anderson v. Weyerhaeuser Co.
questions: Richard Anderson suffered an on the job injury while working as a logger for Weyerhaeuser. He claims the Department of Labor and Industries improperly denied him vocational rehabilitation (i.e., job training), as part of his workers’ compensation claim, without first providing him notice and a hearing. 1:00 P.M.

title: Sammamish Pointe Homeowners Assn., a Washington non-profit corporation, Plaintiff, v. Sammamish Pointe L.L.C. a Washington limited liability company; Polygon Northwest Co., a Washington general partnership; Brentview , a Washington corporation, Respondents, Jeffrey Gow and Jane Doe Gow, individuals and their marital community; Gary Young and Jane Doe Young, individuals and their marital community; Greg Arms and Jane Doe Arms, individuals and their marital community, Defendants, LSP Corp., doing business in unknown form; LSP Specialty Products Co., a Texas corp.; LSP Products Group , a Nevada corp.; Specialty Products; doing business in unknown form; Tech Specialties, doing business in unknown form; Rapid-Fit, doing business in unknown form; Aqua-Flo, a Texas corp.; and John and Mary Does, seven through two hundred, Petitioners
questions: Does a party have to strictly comply or substantially comply with the appropriate statutes to give the court jurisdiction over out of state defendants? If a summons served on an out of state defendant is defective, may a plaintiff amend the summons? Should attorney fees be awarded?

title: McGinnis v. State of Washington
questions: Did the Legislature properly enact a retroactive amendment to the Industrial Welfare Act in 2003 to clarify that public employers are excluded from coverage and were public employers subject to the pre-2003 version of the Act?

title: Zuver v. Airtouch Communications, Inc.
questions: This case requires the Supreme Court to consider whether an arbitration agreement between an employer and employee is unenforceable because some of its provisions are unconscionable.

title: Adler v. Fred Lind Manor
questions: This case requires the Supreme Court to consider whether an arbitration agreement between an employer and employee is unenforceable because some of its provisions are unconscionable and whether this employee waived his right to a jury trial by signing the agreement.

title: Gary Locke v. Sam Reed
questions: The petitioners maintain that legislation establishing a replacement system for this fall’s primary election, as signed into law by the Governor, is not subject to a referendum vote.

title: In re Disciplinary Proceeding Against DeRuiz
State of Washington v. Teal
questions: Whether the State proved all of the elements of first degree robbery where a “to convict” jury instruction only referred to the acts of the defendant and not to the acts of the defendant or an accomplice.

title: State of Washington v. Costich
questions: The State took Mr. Phillip Costich’s property by eminent domain and made an offer to settle the dispute. The court considers the validity of that offer and whether Mr. Costich was entitled to an award of reasonable attorney fees and expert witness fees.

title: State of Washington v. Bradshaw
questions: Should this court overrule a prior decision that holds that knowledge or intent is not an element of unlawful possession of a controlled substance?

title: Spokane County v. Specialty Auto & Truck Painting, Inc.
questions: A Washington court rule prevents a plaintiff who twice dismissed a case involving the same matter and same defendant from filing a third lawsuit against the defendant on that matter. The Court decides whether a stipulated dismissal or court ordered dismissal triggers this “two dismissal” rule.

title: Bianca Faust, individually and as guardian of Gary C. Faust, a minor, and Bianca Celestine Mele, Bryan Mele, Beverly Mele, and Albert Mele, Respondents, v. Bellingham Lodge #493, Loyal Order of Moose , Alexis Chapman, and Moose International , Petitioners, And Mark Albertson, as Personal Administrator for the Estate of Hawkeye Kincaid, deceased, Additional Defendant
questions: A Washington court rule prevents a plaintiff who twice dismissed a case involving the same matter and same defendant from filing a third lawsuit against the defendant on that matter. The Court decides whether a stipulated dismissal or court ordered dismissal triggers this “two dismissal” rule.

title: State of Washington v. Carneh
questions: Leemah Carneh stands charged with four counts of aggravated first degree murder. He has pleaded not guilty by reason of insanity. The question before the court is whether Mr. Carneh may refuse to answer potentially incriminating questions during a mental health evaluation by State experts.

title: State of Washington v. Pete
questions: Whether a new trial is warranted because two documents, which were not admitted into evidence at trial, were inadvertently submitted to the jury.

title: State of Washington v. Harner
questions: Whether the unavailability of a drug court in the county where the defendant was prosecuted violated the defendant’s constitutional guarantees of equal protection and due process.

title: State of Washington v. Keithley
questions: Whether the unavailability of a drug court in the county where the defendant was prosecuted violated the defendant’s constitutional guarantees of equal protection and due process.

title: In re An, Attorney at Law
Diehl v. State of Washington
questions: Mr. Diehl appealed a growth management hearings board decision in superior court. Does he have to follow the same procedural rules as if he were filing a civil suit?

title: Antonius v. King County
questions: Should the court use the federal analysis for deciding whether under state law an employer may be liable in a hostile work environment sex-based discrimination action for acts occurring more than three years before suit is filed?

title: State of Washington v. Christensen
questions: The mother of Christensen’s girlfriend eavesdropped on a conversation he and his girlfriend had using a cordless phone. Did this violate Washington’s privacy act?

title: In re An, Attorney at Law
In re An, Attorney at Law
In re An, Attorney at Law
State of Washington v. Nevarez
questions: Whether law enforcement officers must conduct searches of vehicle occupants at the first opportunity after the officer sees a movement or action by a vehicle occupant that creates an officer safety concern. 1:00 P.M.
